sentences.text: Morrowglass validates each medication order for patient, product, dose, route, and timing fields before making it available for downstream processing.
Copperfield confirms that the reconciliation queue has no unresolved discrepancy before authorizing routine cabinet replenishment.
Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot uses the Order Reconciliation Snapshot to compare requested quantities with completed dispense events and current cabinet balances.
Reconciliation compares the active order record with dispensing and cabinet records using a stable order identifier.
The comparison preserves the order context needed to distinguish a new request from a correction or a repeat submission.
Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot retains the patient, medication, dose, route, and timing details associated with each order while preparing a dispense transaction.
It also checks whether the order is active and whether its authorization remains valid at the time of processing.
A cancelled order is excluded from routine preparation even when a matching dispense request remains in a local queue.
A corrected order is treated as a new authoritative version, and superseded values are not carried forward.
Duplicate submissions are flagged for review rather than converted into additional cabinet quantity.
Partial dispensing is reconciled against the quantity already recorded so that remaining quantity is calculated conservatively.
Time stamps and transaction identifiers are retained to support comparison across records that arrive at different times.
When the records disagree on patient, medication, or quantity, the affected transaction remains on hold until the discrepancy is resolved.
The reconciliation outcome records the matched values, unresolved differences, and disposition for subsequent audit.
North Ward Cabinet Controller applies the North Ward medication access rules when evaluating a cabinet transaction.
Its ward-specific configuration defines permitted medication locations, access roles, and transaction limits for each cabinet.
The configuration associates each medication location with the product identifiers and quantity thresholds used by the ward.
Cabinet availability is calculated from the last confirmed inventory count and subsequent recorded movements.
Configured maximum and minimum quantities guide replenishment decisions without overriding an active clinical restriction.
Access rules require an authenticated user role appropriate to the requested medication and transaction type.
High-risk medication locations can require an additional confirmation before a removal is accepted.
The controller rejects a transaction when its location mapping does not match the reconciled medication identity.
Configuration changes are versioned, reviewed, and recorded with the effective time and approving authority.
If the controller has not received a current approved configuration, it prevents routine dispensing and reports the condition for investigation.
